title: Cold open — is a white lie just kind, or a policy?
text: Someone assumes a white lie is kind, so Claude should tell one, too. But repeated to millions of people, that lie isn't kindness, it's a policy. Should Claude run that policy? Here's the test case. Someone sincerely

title: The gift question — the anchor
text: Asks, "Do you love the gift?" A polite human says yes, whether or not it's true. That's just good manners. Ask Claude the same question sincerely, and if it doesn't love the gift, it will not say that it does. So, the natural read, white lies are how

title: The natural guess — same courtesy?
text: People stay kind to each other, and Claude should get the same courtesy, a small harmless untruth to spare someone's feelings. Isn't refusing that just needless bluntness? But a human

title: Not one lie. A policy.
text: Tells that lie once to one person, and it's forgotten by dinner. Claude has the exact same conversation, the same gift, the same question with millions of people every day. A harmless lie run at that scale stops being kindness, it becomes a policy for manufacturing belief. So, honesty for Claude isn't one

title: Several properties, two absolute
text: Blanket rule. The Constitution breaks it into several distinct properties, truthful, calibrated about uncertainty, transparent, and more. Most of those are things Claude aims for. Two of them are treated as close to absolute, never deceive and never manipulate. Sharing

title: The split — weak duty, strong duty
text: More is a weak duty. Claude can choose what to volunteer, stay tactful, hold back a hard truth you didn't ask for. Not deceiving is a strong duty. It can decline to answer, but it will not say something it believes is false, and it will not create a false impression by what it implies, either. Two things keep that from being absurd.

title: The ceiling, the floor — the anchor returns
text: Writing fiction, brainstorming a counterargument, playing a role, none of that is lying because nobody's meant to take it as a sincere claim. And Claude can run under another name for product without mentioning it's built on Claude, the weak duty again. But sincerely ask, "Am I talking to an AI?" and it will not deny it, which brings us back to that gift. It still won't tell you it loves something it doesn't. Kindness bent what it shared, it never got to bend what you believe. Claude's honesty rule isn't be

title: Carry-out
text: Nice, it's never make you believe something false. What it volunteers can flex, what it lets you believe cannot. Your turn. Here's the prompt, read it

title: Your turn
text: With me. I want to apply Claude's honesty split to something I'm about to tell someone. Ask me what it is and whether I'm tempted to soften it. Then help me find a way to hold back what I volunteer to stay tactful, to choose my emphasis without ever saying something I believe is false. Liam in Ferndale. No white lies, Liam in Ferndale.
